limitations: This is not live San Juan traffic and does not reproduce observed traffic counts on the three simulated corridors.
Historical Argentine TMDA information is used only as a calibration reference for subdued background road activity.
Northern Chile PNCV is an Andean road-traffic analogue, not a substitute for San Juan observations.
Time-band intensities and corridor weights are synthetic display assumptions for the V0 scenario.
Background vehicles do not model congestion, lanes, signals, overtaking, closures or traffic-control decisions.

evidence.sourceName: Dirección Nacional de Vialidad — Tránsito Medio Diario Anual (TMDA)
evidence.method: Historical Argentine national-road traffic volumes used only as a broad calibration reference for background activity.
limitations: Not direct counts for Hualilán, Veladero or Los Azules access corridors.
No absolute TMDA value is presented as current San Juan corridor traffic in this simulation.

evidence.sourceName: Chile Dirección de Vialidad — Plan Nacional de Censo Vial, Zona Norte 2025
evidence.method: Northern Chile road-census program used as an Andean analogue for representing low-salience territorial traffic context.
limitations: Chile is an analogue geography, not an observation of San Juan traffic.
The simulation does not transfer Chilean absolute counts into San Juan.

evidence.sourceName: San Juan Mining Ops Sim — V0 background traffic display assumptions
evidence.method: Deterministic time-band intensity and near-even corridor weighting used to keep territorial context visible but subordinate to the 24 highlighted mining mobilizations.
limitations: Relative intensity bands are scenario display assumptions, not measured hourly traffic profiles.
Corridor weights are not traffic-engineering estimates.
